chatter: Not much doing out here. Wind's picking up off the flats. Smells like a battery fire, which, to be fair, it usually is.
You can see the haze rolling in over the left-field wall. They painted a distance marker on it once. Nobody's ever reached it. Nobody ever will.
Fun fact: this ballpark was built on a landfill, and on humid nights you can still smell every decision that led us here.
{pitcher} out there on the mound looking like a man who owes money to everyone in this stadium. Which, in fairness, he might.
The grounds crew tried to reseed the infield last spring. It came up brown and angry and now they just rake it and apologize.
I'm told the record for longest game at this park is fourteen hours. Seven people finished it. Two of them on purpose.
Somebody in the bleachers just took their shirt off. It's nine degrees out. I'm not going to editorialize, but I have concerns.
Weather's holding, which around here means the acid's only a light drizzle. Bring an umbrella, lose an umbrella. That's the deal.
They sell a hot dog here called the Widowmaker. It comes with a waiver. I've had three.
Little-known stat: no left-handed batter has hit safely at this park after sundown since the lights started flickering. Draw your own conclusions.
The {team} bullpen's been quiet. Then again, half of them are asleep and one of them, I believe, is technically deceased.
Quiet moment out here. Good time to mention the bathrooms are out of order. All of them. Have been since the last administration.
You know, my ex-wife loved this game. Sat right there in section nine. Section nine is a crater now. Life comes at you fast.
Ballpark organist is playing something in a minor key again. He only knows the one song. It's about drowning.
Vendor just walked past selling something he called "meat adjacent." I didn't follow up. I value what's left of me.
The stadium clock froze at 6:66 four years ago and honestly it's never been wrong about the mood.
Somewhere out past the outfield wall a dog is howling in perfect rhythm with the crowd. Nobody brought a dog.
They retired a number here once. Not for a player. For a guy who survived a full season in the cheap seats. Brave soul.
Folks ask me who Sir Charles was. He owned this ground. Halcyon offered him a fortune for it three times, and three times he sent the cheque back with two tickets in the envelope.
People rub the shoes on the Sir Charles statue out front for luck. The shoes are gold now. The luck's still bronze.
They keep Sir Charles's seat behind home plate empty. Nobody sits in it. Not even the drunks, and that's saying something.
Halcyon built a whole estate round this ballpark because Sir Charles wouldn't sell. You can still see the offices sulking over the left-field wall.
The Coldwater Basin Blue Birds are the oldest club in this league. They were playing ball in Old Coldwater when the Meridian still had a doorman.
The Coldwater Crows go back to 2022, before the Curtain went up. One club in this league is older, and the Crows have spent every season since trying to bury it.
Blue Birds and Crows. Oldest grudge in the Basin. Nobody remembers what started it, and everybody remembers whose side they're on.
Sir Charles was a Blue Birds man. Never missed a home game, never said a kind word about the Crows, and the Crows have never said one back.
Never been a wire in a Crows uniform. Not one augment, not one graft, not since 2022. Ask them why and they just smile at you. Politely. For a long time.
The Crows don't sign free agents. Somebody vouches for you, you sit a season in the stands, and one day there's a jersey in your locker. Nobody ever says who left it.
You'll see crows on the light towers on game nights. Just sitting. Watching. The Crows' people say that's lucky. They don't say for who.

intro: Good evening, wasteland, and welcome to DEADBALL. Chip Vega in the booth, and we've got nine innings of ball for whoever's still got working eyes.
Chip Vega here at the ballpark, where the lights work maybe sixty percent of the time and the hot dogs are legally a dare. Let's play ball.
This is DEADBALL on Coldwater League radio. I'm Chip Vega. Somewhere out there the sun's setting on a stadium that has definitely, definitely been condemned.
Welcome back to the ballgame. Chip Vega, and I'll be your only friend for the next nine innings.
Good evening from the Charles B. Hughson Coliseum. Chip Vega in the booth, and Sir Charles is out front in bronze, same as every night.

On the marquee: {away} versus {home}. Two rosters, one working scoreboard, no medical staff.
The {away} take the field against the {home}. Bad blood, worse plumbing. Here we go.
It's {home} hosting {away} under whatever's left of the stadium lights.

It's {home} ({homeRecord}) hosting {away} ({awayRecord}), two clubs clawing up a league table nobody escapes.
outro: That's DEADBALL. {leader} take the day. Chip Vega saying: go home, lock the door, and dream of extra innings.
For the {leader} and everyone still upright out there, this has been Chip Vega. Good night, and mind the radiation.
Chip Vega, signing off. Same dirt, same dread, tomorrow. Stay off the field.

worldseries.intro: This is it. THE CURTAIN CALL. One game, two clubs, and a whole miserable season of baseball comes down to the next nine innings. Chip Vega, and I have never been more awake.
Welcome to the DEADBALL CURTAIN CALL. Winner takes the crown, loser takes the long walk home. Chip Vega in the booth, gripping the desk so hard my knuckles went.
Nine innings from immortality. The Curtain Call, folks. Last game of the season, and somebody's about to become a legend in a town that forgets fast.
They call it the Curtain Call because it's the last act of the season, and because the Curtain is the one thing in this city nobody's knocked down. Yet. Chip Vega, let's go.

The {away} ({awayRecord}) against the {home} ({homeRecord}), the two best clubs left standing, playing for the only thing that ever mattered.
Winner takes the season, loser takes nothing. {away} and {home}. Let's settle it.
